No two consecutive words can share the same first letter. Write a descriptive, fictional, imaginative screenplay of a fish being pulled out of the water by a human and made to stare at the solar eclipse. The fish descends into a lovecraftian monologue about "horrors beyond it's comprehension" and has an existensial crisisassistant
response:
FADE IN:

EXT. BEACH - DAY

The sun beats down on the sandy shore as a human, JEN (30s), wades into the ocean, her eyes scanning the water for signs of life. Suddenly, she spots a fish, FINLEY (a sleek, silver fish), swimming near the surface. She reaches out a hand, and Finley is sucked into her grasp.

Jen holds Finley up, admiring the fish's scales as the sun beats down on them. But then, she notices the approaching solar eclipse. The sky darkens, and the air cools.

JEN
(awed)
Oh, look! A solar eclipse!

Finley, now trapped in Jen's hand, begins to struggle and squirm. As the moon passes between the earth and the sun, the light in the water begins to distort and writhe.

FINLEY
(whispering)
No... no... this is not right...

Jen, oblivious to Finley's distress, continues to marvel at the eclipse. But Finley's eyes are fixed on the darkening sky, and his mind is reeling.

FINLEY
(whispering)
The void... it's coming... the void...

Finley's voice rises to a frantic whisper as the eclipse reaches its peak.

FINLEY
(whispering)
Horrors beyond my comprehension... eldritch abominations... crawling, twisting, writhing... the very fabric of reality unraveling...

Jen, still entranced by the eclipse, doesn't notice Finley's transformation. But as the fish's monologue grows more intense, his body begins to contort and twist, his scales shimmering with an otherworldly energy.

FINLEY
(whispering)
I am but a mere mortal... a fleeting thought in the grand tapestry of existence... and yet... and yet... I am bound to this... this... this prison...

Finley's voice drops to a mere whisper, and his eyes roll back in his head. He begins to speak in a language that sounds like the rustling of leaves and the creaking of wooden ships.

FINLEY
(whispering)
The abyssal void... it calls to me... a siren's song of madness and despair... I am but a mere fish... a insignificant speck in the grand scheme of things...

As the eclipse reaches its end, Finley's body begins to dissolve, his scales shimmering with an eerie, ethereal light. Jen, still entranced by the eclipse, doesn't notice the transformation.

JEN
(awed)
Oh, look! The sun is coming back!

Finley's voice, now a mere echo, whispers one final phrase.

FINLEY
(whispering)
I am no more...

The camera lingers on Finley's dissolving form as the sun re-emerges from behind the moon. The beach is bathed in a warm, golden light, but Finley is gone, lost in the abyss of his own existential crisis.

FADE TO BLACK.

FADE IN:

EXT. BEACH - LATER

Jen, still entranced by the eclipse, wanders along the beach, lost in thought. She stumbles upon a piece of paper, partially buried in the sand. It's a fragment of Finley's monologue, scrawled in a madman's handwriting.

JEN
(reads)
"Horrors beyond my comprehension... eldritch abominations... crawling, twisting, writhing... the very fabric of reality unraveling..."

Jen looks up, a shiver running down her spine. She realizes that Finley was more than just a fish – he was a vessel for something ancient, something eldritch.

Jen's eyes widen as she understands the true horror of the solar eclipse. The void is not just a phenomenon of the universe – it's a doorway to madness, a portal to the abyss.

FADE TO BLACK.

THE END.
